_source: Pasco County Land Development Code (LDC), Comprehensive Plan, and Fee Schedules
_jurisdiction: Pasco County (Unincorporated). Incorporated areas governed by City of New Port Richey, City of Port Richey, City of Zephyrhills, or City of Dade City codes.
_note: Fees and requirements current as of 2025. Verify all fees and standards with Pasco County Development Services (727-847-8137) or the Pasco County LDC at library.municode.com. Impact fees are subject to annual CPI adjustments.
authority:
Pasco County, Florida — Development Services Department
Unincorporated Pasco County: governed by the Pasco County Land Development Code (LDC) and Comprehensive Plan.
Incorporated municipalities: City of New Port Richey, City of Port Richey, City of Zephyrhills, and City of Dade City each adopt their own land development regulations.
Contact: Pasco County Development Services | 8731 Citizens Drive, Suite 100, New Port Richey, FL 34654 | (727) 847-8137 | pascogov.com/building
passenger_loading:
Pasco County LDC Section 500.3 — Parking Requirements by Use
Single-Family Residential: 2 spaces/unit (min)
Multi-Family (1 BR): 1.5 spaces/unit | Multi-Family (2+ BR): 2.0 spaces/unit
Office/Professional: 3.5 spaces per 1,000 sf GFA
Retail/Commercial: 4.0–5.0 spaces per 1,000 sf GFA
Restaurant (General): 1 space per 75 sf of dining area, or 10 spaces per 1,000 sf
Medical/Dental Office: 5.0 spaces per 1,000 sf GFA
Warehouse/Industrial: 1 space per 1,000 sf GFA (min 2 spaces)
Bicycle Parking: Required on commercial/multi-family sites — minimum 5% of required vehicle spaces or 2 spaces, whichever is greater
Loading: Commercial/Industrial — 1 berth for first 10,000 sf GFA; 1 additional per each 20,000 sf thereafter
Verify use-specific requirements with Pasco County LDC Section 500.3.
stall_dimensions:
Pasco County LDC Section 500.3
90-degree stall: 9 ft wide × 18 ft deep (min); drive aisle 24 ft (two-way) or 22 ft (one-way)
60-degree angled stall: 9 ft wide × 18 ft deep; drive aisle 18 ft (one-way)
45-degree angled stall: 9 ft wide × 18 ft deep; drive aisle 14 ft (one-way)
ADA Accessible: 8 ft stall + 5 ft access aisle (standard) or 8 ft stall + 8 ft access aisle (van accessible)
ADA Count: 1 per 1–25 total spaces; 2 per 26–50; 3 per 51–75; 4 per 76–100; 1 per 50 thereafter (per ADA Standards)
Van-accessible ADA: 1 per 6 required ADA spaces (min 1)
Compact spaces: Not permitted to satisfy required parking counts
All parking stalls and drives must be paved (asphalt or concrete) and properly drained.
shared_parking:
Pasco County LDC Section 500.3.3 — Shared Parking
Shared parking agreements are permitted between uses with non-overlapping peak demand hours. A parking study demonstrating demand offsets must be submitted. A recorded cross-access/shared parking easement and agreement between property owners is required.
Contact Pasco County Development Services for shared parking study methodology and approval process.
landscape_req:
Pasco County LDC Chapter 500, Article VII — Landscaping
Vehicular Use Areas (VUA): Minimum interior landscaping equal to 5% of total VUA; 1 canopy/shade tree (min 10 ft tall, 2.5-inch caliper at install) per 10 parking spaces; 4-ft landscape strip at all parking lot perimeters abutting rights-of-way.
Buffer Yards: Required between incompatible land uses per LDC Article VII; width and plant density vary by adjacency type (e.g., commercial adjacent to residential).
Foundation/Building Landscaping: Required for all non-residential buildings; shrubs/groundcover minimum 18 inches tall at install along building facades facing public ROW.
Street Trees: 1 canopy tree per 35–50 linear feet of ROW frontage (species from approved Pasco County list).
Irrigation: Required automated irrigation system for all required landscaping on commercial sites.
Plant Material: All landscaping must use drought-tolerant, Florida-Friendly species from the Pasco County approved plant list.
tree_survey:
Pasco County LDC Article VII — Tree Preservation and Permit Requirements
Tree Removal Permit required for any regulated tree (generally >8 inches DBH on commercial/multi-family; any tree on residential) prior to land clearing or development.
Tree Preservation: Pasco County requires a tree survey for sites with trees ≥4 inches DBH. Grand trees (≥18 inches DBH for most species) receive heightened protection.
Mitigation: Removal of protected trees requires mitigation through replacement planting on-site or payment into the Pasco County Tree Bank at the rate established in the current fee schedule.
Consult Pasco County Environmental Lands Program: (727) 847-8137.
Verify requirements with the Pasco County Natural Resources Division before any land clearing.
signage:
Pasco County LDC Article IX — Sign Regulations (Unincorporated)
Freestanding Ground Signs: Maximum 1 per street frontage; height limit varies by zoning district (typically 8–15 ft); sign area typically 50–150 sf depending on zone.
Wall Signs: Generally limited to 10–15% of building wall area facing a public street (max ~150 sf typical commercial).
Electronic Message Center (EMC): Permitted in C-2, C-3, I-1, I-2 districts with constraints on animation/flash interval (min 8-second static hold).
Temporary Signs: Model home, real estate, and construction signs governed by LDC Article IX with size and duration limits.
Permit: A sign permit is required for most permanent signage; submit to Pasco County Building Department.
Verify site-specific restrictions with Pasco LDC Article IX and the specific zoning district standards.
platting:
Pasco County LDC Chapter 200 — Subdivisions and Platting
Subdivision plat required for any division of land into 3 or more parcels, or when new ROW dedication is required.
Minor Subdivision (2 lots, no new ROW): Administrative review; may be processed as lot split.
Major Subdivision: Full plat process — pre-application meeting, preliminary plat, Board of County Commissioners (BCC) approval, final plat recording.
Concurrency review required for transportation, schools, utilities, and recreation (Chapter 200).
Contact Pasco County Development Services: (727) 847-8137 | Engineering/Land Development Division.
utilities:
Water: Pasco County Utilities (PCU) serves most of unincorporated Pasco County. Contact: (727) 847-2411 | pascogov.com/pcu
Sewer: PCU provides sanitary sewer in served areas. Septic/OSTDS may be permitted in rural areas (Pasco County Health Department approval required).
Reclaimed Water: PCU has reclaimed water service in many areas; required for irrigation in served zones.
Electric: TECO/Peoples Gas (gas) | Duke Energy or TECO (electric) depending on location.
Storm Water: Pasco County Stormwater/Utilities Division | (727) 847-8032
Note: Verify utility availability and capacity with each provider prior to development. Extension agreements and capacity reservation fees apply.
impact_studies:
Traffic Study: Required if site generates ≥100 net new peak-hour trips (PM peak) per the Pasco County Concurrency Management System. ITE Trip Generation Manual shall be used for calculations.
Natural Resource Assessment (NRA): May be required for sites with potential wetlands, listed species habitat, or flood-prone areas per Pasco LDC.
Geotechnical Report: Required for new structures; sinkhole assessment (ASTM D6285 Standard) typically required in Pasco County due to karst terrain.
FEMA Flood Study: Required if site is in SFHA (AE, AH, VE zones); baseline flood elevation certification and No-Rise analysis may apply.
Contact Pasco County Development Services and Environmental Lands for required studies.
storm_treatment:
Southwest Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD): ERP required for any ground disturbance triggering SWFWMD thresholds (generally >1 acre disturbed or any wetland impact). Contact: 1-800-423-1476 | swfwmd.state.fl.us
Pasco County Stormwater: Local stormwater management review per Pasco County LDC Chapter 400 — Stormwater Management. Retention/detention required; treatment standard: 1-inch over impervious area (SWFWMD) or as specified by Pasco Engineering.
Flood Plain Management: FEMA NFIP participant; development in AE/AH zones requires finished floors at or above BFE + 1 ft freeboard per Pasco County floodplain ordinance.
Best Management Practices (BMPs): Required for construction phase NPDES — prepare SWPPP and file NOI with FDEP if ≥1 acre disturbed.
wetlands_flood:
Pasco County contains significant wetlands and is located within SWFWMD jurisdiction. Wetland impacts require SWFWMD Environmental Resource Permit (ERP) and may require USACE Section 404 Permit.
FEMA Flood Zones: Substantial portions of Pasco County are in SFHA (Zone AE) or moderate-risk (Zone X-shaded). Verify flood zone at msc.fema.gov.
Coastal High Hazard Area (CHHA): Portions of western Pasco County are designated CHHA; evacuations zones and density restrictions apply per the Pasco County Comprehensive Plan.
Natural Resource Assessment recommended prior to site plan; contact Pasco County Environmental Lands (727) 847-8137.
geotechnical:
Pasco County is located in an active karst region (Central Florida). Sinkhole risk is moderate-to-high.
A geotechnical investigation with sinkhole assessment is strongly recommended (and typically required by lenders/insurers) prior to development.
Sinkhole assessment per ASTM D6285 or Florida Subsurface Utility Engineering standards; ground-penetrating radar (GPR) or standard penetration testing (SPT) borings typically used.
Compressive strength, bearing capacity, and groundwater depth data required for foundation design.
Pasco County Building Dept. will require geotechnical report as part of building permit submittal for structures.
traffic_study:
Pasco County Concurrency Management: Required if project generates ≥100 net new PM peak-hour trips (ITE manual). Pasco County Level of Service (LOS) standard: LOS D on most arterials; LOS C on some collectors.
Coordinate with Pasco County MPO (Metropolitan Planning Organization) for large-scale projects.
FDOT District 7: Driveway connection permit required for access to state roads (US-19, SR-52, SR-54, SR-56, etc.); (813) 975-6000.
Transportation Impact Fee credit may be available for existing uses or prior commitments.
building_code:
2023 Florida Building Code (FBC), 7th Edition — Residential and Commercial
Florida Building Code — Existing Building, Accessibility, Energy Conservation, and Plumbing/Mechanical/Fuel Gas also apply.
Pasco County has no local amendments beyond the base FBC (verify at time of permit).
Building Permit required for all new construction, additions, and renovations. Submit to Pasco County Building Services: 8731 Citizens Drive, Suite 100, New Port Richey, FL 34654 | (727) 847-8137.
Electrical: NEC (NFPA 70) as adopted by FBC. Plumbing: FBC Plumbing. Fire: NFPA 1 and NFPA 101 (Life Safety Code) as adopted by Florida Fire Prevention Code.
construction_methods:
Sinkhole Risk: Moderate-to-high throughout Pasco County (karst terrain). Geotechnical investigation with sinkhole screening required before construction; engineered foundations (drilled piers, ground improvement) may be needed.
Coastal High Hazard Area (CHHA): Portions of western/coastal Pasco County (Gulf of Mexico coast) — CHHA construction standards, freeboard requirements, and FEMA flood-resistant construction apply.
Wind: Pasco County is in ASCE 7 Wind Speed Zone; verify design wind speed for site using Florida Product Approval map. Most sites: 130–140 mph design wind.
High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ): Pasco County is NOT in HVHZ but standard FBC wind provisions apply.
Flood: Structures in SFHA must be elevated per FEMA/FBC requirements; lowest floor at BFE + 1 ft (residential) per Pasco County amendments.
fire_route:
Pasco County Fire Rescue: Coordinate access and fire hydrant requirements with Pasco County Fire Rescue during site plan review. Contact: (727) 847-8031.
Fire access roadway: Minimum 20 ft clear width (24 ft preferred), capable of supporting 85,000 lb fire apparatus, with vertically clear 13.5 ft.
Hydrant spacing: Commercial — within 300 ft of all exterior walls; Industrial — within 400 ft. Hydrant flow: minimum 1,500 GPM for commercial.
Fire sprinkler system: Required for new commercial buildings >7,500 sf and multi-family ≥3 stories per Florida Fire Prevention Code / Pasco County ordinance. Verify current thresholds with Pasco County Fire Marshal.
Fire lane posting and marking required per NFPA 1.
impact_fees:
Pasco County Impact Fees (effective July 1, 2024; subject to annual adjustment)
Transportation Impact Fee: Varies by land use and location. Example rates per sf GFA or unit:
  — Single Family: $7,400–$12,500/unit (varies by home size tier)
  — Multi-Family: $4,500–$7,000/unit
  — Retail (General): $14.00–$20.00/sf GFA
  — Office: $7.00–$11.00/sf GFA
  — Industrial/Warehouse: $3.00–4.50/sf GFA
School Impact Fee (Pasco County School District): ~$5,000–$8,500/residential unit (varies by type/size)
Fire/EMS Impact Fee: ~$400–$900/unit or equivalent commercial fee
Parks/Recreation Impact Fee: ~$1,200–$2,500/residential unit
Library Impact Fee: ~$200–$500/residential unit
Note: Impact fees are paid at building permit issuance. Verify current rates with Pasco County Impact Fee office: (727) 847-8137 | pascogov.com/developmentservices
application_fees:
Pasco County Development Services — Application Fees (FY2024–2025; verify current schedule)
Site Plan Review: $500–$5,000+ depending on project scope and acreage
Zoning Variances / Special Exceptions: $500–$1,500
CUP (Conditional Use Permit): $750–$2,000
Rezoning (LDC Text Amendment): $1,500–$3,000
Building Permit (Commercial): 1.0% of construction value (min $100)
Demolition Permit: $100–$500
ROW Use Permit / Excavation: $200–$500
Tree Removal Permit: $50–$200 + mitigation fee if applicable
Sign Permit: $50–$300
Flood Zone Determination/LOMA: $150
Contact Pasco County Building Services: (727) 847-8137 | pascogov.com/building
dedication:
ROW dedication may be required as a condition of development approval for road widening or new road connection. Pasco County Engineering will determine ROW needs based on adopted roadway cross-sections.
Conservation/Drainage Easements may be required for SWFWMD compliance and stormwater management.
Contact Pasco County Engineering and Planning for project-specific dedication requirements.
securities:
Landscape/Utility Improvement Bond or Letter of Credit: Required for off-site improvements and landscaping at final plat or prior to CO issuance (amount = 110% of estimated cost).
Water/Sewer Connection Fees (Pasco County Utilities):
  — Water Meter (3/4-inch residential): ~$2,200–$3,500
  — Water Meter (1-inch commercial): ~$3,500–$6,000
  — Sewer Connection (residential unit): ~$2,500–$4,500
  — Capacity Reservation Fee: determined by PCU based on projected demand
Contact PCU for current connection fee schedule: (727) 847-2411.
lot_line:
Lot Line Adjustment (Minor): Administrative review if no new lots/ROW are created. Fee: approximately $200–$400.
Lot Split (2 lots, no new ROW): Minor Subdivision process; administrative review.
Plat Vacation/Replat: Requires BCC approval; fees vary.
Verify requirements with Pasco County Development Services — Planning Division: (727) 847-8137.
pre_app:
Pre-Application Conference: Available through Pasco County Development Services. Strongly recommended for projects requiring rezoning, site plan, or special exceptions.
Schedule via: (727) 847-8137 or pascogov.com/developmentservices
Pre-Application fee: $100–$300 (may be credited toward application fee).
Pasco County also offers a Development Assistance Center (DAC) for over-the-counter intake and early technical guidance.
coastal_dev_permit:
Western Pasco County (Gulf Coast): Portions of Pasco County abut the Gulf of Mexico. CHHA and CCCL (Coastal Construction Control Line) may apply.
Florida DEP CCCL Permit required for construction within or seaward of the CCCL (via FDEP Division of Water Resource Management).
Pasco County does not have a separate Coastal Development Permit but requires CHHA analysis in the site plan for designated coastal areas.
Boating/dock permits: FDEP / USACE / Pasco County Environmental Lands coordination required for waterway structures.
Contact FDEP Southwest District: (813) 632-7600.
lot_line_adj_timing:
Lot Line Adjustment: 2–4 weeks (administrative review if no new ROW or lots created).
Minor Subdivision (lot split): 4–6 weeks.
Major Subdivision / Plat: 3–6 months (preliminary plat through final plat and BCC approval).
entitlements:
Rezoning / FLUM Amendment (small scale, <10 acres): 3–6 months; BCC public hearing required.
Conditional Use Permit (CUP): 2–4 months; BCC or Hearing Officer public hearing.
Site Plan (Permitted Use, no rezoning): 4–10 weeks administrative review.
Variance (Zoning Board of Appeals): 4–8 weeks.
DRI (Development of Regional Impact, if applicable): 12–24 months.
Note: All rezoning and land use amendments require a Pasco County Planning Commission recommendation followed by BCC action.
perm_steps:
1. Pre-Application Conference (recommended): Schedule with Pasco County Development Services.
2. Concurrency Application: Submit for transportation, schools, utilities, and recreation concurrency review.
3. Site Plan Application: Submit to Development Services with engineering, landscape, drainage plans.
4. DRC (Development Review Committee) review and comments.
5. Site Plan Approval / Conditions of Approval issued.
6. Submit for any required Environmental Resource Permit (SWFWMD).
7. Building Permit Application: Submit construction documents to Pasco County Building Services.
8. Building Inspections during construction.
9. Final Inspection + Certificate of Occupancy (CO) issued.
Note: Tree removal permit, sign permit, and ROW permit must be obtained separately before/during construction phase.
local_permits:
Pasco County Building Services: (727) 847-8137 | 8731 Citizens Drive, Suite 100, New Port Richey, FL 34654
Building Permit Review Time: 3–8 weeks for commercial projects (varies with completeness and complexity).
Over-the-Counter permits available for minor residential work at the Development Assistance Center.
Pasco County Inspector Scheduling: MyPermit Pasco portal — mypermit.pascogov.com
EPSS (Electronic Plan Submission): Available for plan submittal and tracking.
wmd:
Southwest Florida Water Management District (SWFWMD)
2379 Broad Street, Brooksville, FL 34604 | 1-800-423-1476 | swfwmd.state.fl.us
Environmental Resource Permit (ERP) required if: total land disturbance ≥1 acre, any wetland impacts, or stormwater system designed to serve commercial or multi-family uses.
Exemptions may apply for small sites with minimal impervious area and no wetland/water impacts.
ERP — Individual Permit (standard): 4–6 months.
ERP — noticed general permit (NGP): 30–90 days.
Well/water use permit may be required for dewatering or on-site water supply.
SWFWMD permitting can typically run concurrently with Pasco County local review.
fdep:
Florida Dept. of Environmental Protection (FDEP) — Southwest District
13051 N Telecom Parkway, Temple Terrace, FL 33637 | (813) 632-7600 | floridadep.gov
Waste Water: Permit required for sanitary sewer collection/transmission system extensions (Notice of Intent — General Permit: ~2 months).
Water Main Extension: Notice of Intent to Pasco County Utilities / FDEP.
NPDES Construction Site Stormwater: FDEP Generic Permit for Stormwater Discharge from Large/Small Construction Activities — file NOI if ≥1 acre disturbed.
Contaminated Sites: Review Phase I/II ESA findings; notify FDEP Contaminated Site Program if contamination confirmed.
CCCL (Coastal Construction Control Line): FDEP permit required for coastal Pasco County sites within CCCL.
fdot:
Florida Dept. of Transportation — District 7
11201 N McKinley Drive, Tampa, FL 33612 | (813) 975-6000 | fdotd7.com
Driveway Connection Permit: Required for access to any State Road (e.g., US-19, US-41, SR-52, SR-54, SR-56, SR-581, CR-54/Gunn Hwy).
Permit timeline: typically 2–4 months. Pre-application meeting with FDOT District 7 Access Management recommended.
Transportation Impact Fee credit available for FDOT road projects in the vicinity.
FDOT Traffic Study: Required if net new PM peak-hour trips exceed applicable FDOT thresholds on a State road.
staff_meetings:
Pre-Application Conference (PAC): Recommended before any rezoning, site plan, or CUP submittal. Schedule via Pasco County Development Services.
Development Review Committee (DRC): Multi-department technical review meeting; attendance typically required for projects with site plan applications. Includes representatives from Planning, Engineering, Fire, Utilities, Building, and Environmental Lands.
Pasco County School District: Concurrency review coordination for residential projects.
SWFWMD Pre-Application Meeting: Recommended for projects with potential wetland or water resource impacts.
public_meetings:
Zoning Board of Adjustment (ZBA): Hears variance applications; monthly public meetings. Applicant presentation and public comment required.
Pasco County Planning Commission (PC): Recommends on rezonings, FLUM amendments, large-scale site plans. Public hearings held approximately monthly.
Board of County Commissioners (BCC): Final approval authority for rezonings, FLUM amendments, CUPs, and plats. Public hearings typically bi-weekly.
Neighborhood Notification: Required for most discretionary approvals; mailed notice to properties within 500 feet.
jurisdictional_authority:
Pasco County Development Services, 8731 Citizens Drive, Suite 100, New Port Richey, FL 34654 | (727) 847-8137
Governing Code: Pasco County Land Development Code (LDC) and Pasco County Comprehensive Plan
Web: pascogov.com/developmentservices
Incorporated areas: City of New Port Richey, City of Port Richey, City of Zephyrhills, or City of Dade City (verify jurisdiction by address).
geotech:
Pasco County lies within central Florida's karst zone — moderate-to-high sinkhole risk. A geotechnical report with sinkhole screening (GPR, SPT borings, or equivalent per ASTM D6285) is typically required for new structures by lenders, insurers, and the building department.
Groundwater depth varies significantly across the county; subsurface investigation should assess bearing capacity, ESHWT (Estimated Seasonal High Water Table), and any karst features.
Contact a licensed geotechnical engineer registered in Florida. Report must be submitted with building permit application.
floodplain:
Verify FEMA flood zone designation at msc.fema.gov (FEMA Map Service Center) using the site address. Pasco County NFIP Community #: 125131.
Zone AE (100-year floodplain with BFE): Finished floor must be at BFE + 1 ft freeboard (Pasco County amendment).
Zone X-Shaded (500-year flood): Minimal regulatory restrictions but evaluate drainage.
Coastal AE/VE zones in western Pasco County: FEMA FIRM and CHHA restrictions apply.
FEMA Elevation Certificate required for structures in SFHA prior to CO.
wetlands:
Pasco County contains Wetlands of Special Significance (WSS). Field delineation by a qualified environmental professional is required. Delineation must be submitted with ERP application to SWFWMD.
Wetland impacts require SWFWMD ERP and typically USACE Section 404 Permit (Nationwide or Individual). Mitigation (on-site preservation, creation, or purchase of mitigation bank credits) required for wetland impacts.
Contact Pasco County Environmental Lands Division: (727) 847-8137.
building_requirements:
Pasco County — 2023 Florida Building Code, 7th Edition governs all new construction, additions, and renovations.
Minimum finished floor elevation for SFHA: BFE + 1 ft (residential) per Pasco County Floodplain Ordinance.
Sinkhole-resistant construction may be required based on geotechnical findings.
Energy Code: Florida Building Code — Energy Conservation (ASHRAE 90.1 or Chapter 13 residential equivalent).
Fire protection: NFPA 1 and NFPA 101 as adopted by Florida Fire Prevention Code.
ADA/Accessibility: ADA Standards for Accessible Design and FBC-Accessibility apply to all public-accommodation and commercial facilities.
Verify site-specific requirements with Pasco County Building Services and the applicable zoning district standards.
chha:
Coastal High Hazard Area (CHHA) in Pasco County: Designated areas along the Gulf Coast in western Pasco County (generally evacuation zones A and B). The Pasco County Comprehensive Plan restricts intensification of residential density in the CHHA.
CHHA Development Standards: New residential development in CHHA requires evaluation against Comprehensive Plan Policy; density increases to non-conforming structures may be restricted.
Flood-resistant construction standards (FEMA / FBC) apply. CHHA parcels must comply with FDEP CCCL requirements if within the CCCL setback.
Verify CHHA designation with Pasco County Planning Division and review Comprehensive Plan Coastal Management Element.
vehicular:
Pasco County LDC Section 500.3 — Vehicular Parking Spaces by Use:
Single-Family: 2 spaces/unit
Duplex: 2 spaces/unit
Multi-Family (studio/1 BR): 1.5 spaces/unit | (2 BR): 2.0/unit | (3+ BR): 2.5/unit
Office (general): 3.5 spaces/1,000 sf GFA
Retail (< 25,000 sf): 4.5 spaces/1,000 sf GFA | (> 25,000 sf): 5.0/1,000 sf
Restaurant: 1 space/75 sf dining area or 10/1,000 sf GFA
Medical/Dental Office: 5.0 spaces/1,000 sf GFA
Industrial/Warehouse: 1.0 space/1,000 sf GFA (min 2)
Hotel/Motel: 1 space/room + 1/employee peak shift
All parking areas must be paved (asphalt or concrete), striped, and drained.
ada:
ADA Accessible Spaces (per ADA Standards for Accessible Design, adopted by Florida) required in all publicly accessible parking areas.
1–25 total spaces: 1 accessible space
26–50: 2 | 51–75: 3 | 76–100: 4 | 101–150: 5 | 151–200: 6 | 201–300: 7 | 301–400: 8 | 401–500: 9
501+: 2% of total spaces
Van-Accessible: 1 in every 6 required accessible spaces (minimum 1 van-accessible per lot)
Stall dimensions: ADA standard: 8 ft + 5 ft access aisle; van-accessible: 8 ft + 8 ft access aisle, or 11 ft wide with adjacent 5 ft aisle
Located closest to accessible building entrance; compliant access route required.
bicycle:
Pasco County LDC Section 500.3 — Bicycle Parking:
Required for commercial, multi-family, and institutional uses.
Minimum: 5% of required vehicular parking spaces, or 2 spaces — whichever is greater.
Bicycle racks must be permanently anchored, located within 100 ft of main building entrance, and shown on site plan.
Covered bicycle parking encouraged for larger facilities (employers, transit hubs).
loading:
Pasco County LDC Section 500.3 — Off-Street Loading Berths:
0–9,999 sf GFA: No loading berth required (unless use requires deliveries)
10,000–49,999 sf GFA: 1 berth
50,000–99,999 sf GFA: 2 berths
100,000+ sf GFA: 3 berths + 1 per additional 100,000 sf
Minimum berth dimensions: 12 ft wide × 35 ft long × 14 ft vertical clearance (semi-truck capable).
Loading areas must not block required parking, driveways, or pedestrian paths.
stall_dim:
Pasco County LDC Section 500.3 — Parking Stall Dimensions:
90-degree: 9 ft wide × 18 ft deep | Two-way drive aisle: 24 ft min | One-way: 22 ft min
60-degree angled: 9 ft × 18 ft | One-way aisle: 18 ft
45-degree angled: 9 ft × 18 ft | One-way aisle: 14 ft
ADA standard: 8 ft + 5 ft access aisle (13 ft total)
ADA van-accessible: 8 ft + 8 ft access aisle (16 ft total) or 11 ft wide with adjacent aisle
All surfaces: paved (asphalt or concrete), properly drained, wheel stops or raised curb at head of stalls near landscaping.
swfwmd_req:
SWFWMD Environmental Resource Permit (ERP) Requirements:
Required when: land disturbance ≥1 acre; wetland/surface water impacts; or stormwater management system for commercial/multi-family development.
Stormwater Treatment Standard: Retain or treat first 1 inch of runoff over entire project site (or volume based on percent impervious), whichever is greater.
Water Quality: Must achieve 80% reduction in annual average load of total suspended solids (TSS).
Floodplain/Floodway: No net fill in the 100-year floodplain; compensatory storage required if fill unavoidable.
Pervious Area Requirements: Maintain or restore pre-development groundwater recharge areas as feasible.
Permit timeline: Noticed General Permit (NGP) — 30–90 days; Individual ERP — 4–6 months.
Contact SWFWMD: 1-800-423-1476 | swfwmd.state.fl.us
city_req:
Pasco County Stormwater Management (Local Requirements):
Pasco County LDC Chapter 400 — Stormwater Management governs local drainage.
Design Storm: 25-year, 24-hour event for on-site retention/detention; 100-year event for downstream conveyance analysis.
Pond/Basin: Wet or dry detention/retention ponds; must be shown on engineering site plan. Side slopes: minimum 4:1 (horizontal to vertical) below control elevation for public safety.
Erosion Control: Silt fences, inlet protection, and SWPPP required during construction.
Outfall: Discharge to Pasco County roadside swales, stormwater systems, or approved water bodies; legal positive outfall must be documented.
Flat Pretreatment: Grease interceptors required for food service uses; calculate size per Florida Plumbing Code / Pasco County Engineering Standards.
Contact: Pasco County Stormwater Engineering: (727) 847-8032.
retention:
Pasco County Stormwater Retention/Detention Standards (LDC Chapter 400):
Retention (dry): Must drain within 72 hours of peak storm event; ESHWT governs recovery rate.
Wet Detention: Permanent pool volume = 2.5 times the treatment volume; littoral zone plantings required around perimeter (minimum 30% of pond perimeter).
Setbacks: Retention ponds at least 15 ft from property lines and structures (verify with site-specific plan).
Outfall Control: Adjustable weir or control structure required to stage drawdown; engineer of record must certify design.
Irrigation offset: Retention ponds used for irrigation may receive stormwater credits per SWFWMD guidelines.
vehicular_areas:
Pasco County LDC Article VII — Vehicular Use Area (VUA) Landscaping:
Interior VUA Landscaping: Minimum 5% of total VUA (parking and drive areas) must be landscaped interior islands.
1 canopy tree (minimum 10 ft tall, 2.5-inch caliper at installation) required per 10 parking spaces.
Island dims: Minimum 8 ft wide and 8 ft long; 5 ft wide with curbing acceptable for narrow situations.
Perimeter buffer: 4-ft wide landscaped strip between parking lot edge and ROW or adjacent property lines.
Tree species: Must be from Pasco County approved tree species list (canopy trees); no prohibited invasive species.
Ground cover: Shrubs, grass, or mulched beds in all landscape islands; no bare soil.
foundation:
Pasco County LDC Article VII — Foundation / Building Perimeter Landscaping:
Required for all non-residential buildings on commercial/industrial sites.
Minimum: Shrubs or groundcover at least 18 inches tall at installation, placed along all building facades facing a public ROW or primary parking area.
Trees: Street trees (canopy) required at 1 per 35–50 linear feet along ROW frontage.
Screening: Dumpster/utility enclosures must be screened on all sides with opaque fencing or masonry walls plus landscaping on exterior.
Hedging and ornamental trees may supplement but do not replace required canopy trees.
All foundation plantings must be maintained in good health per the approved landscape plan.
tree_removal:
Pasco County LDC Article VII — Tree Removal / Permits:
Tree Survey: Required for all commercial/multi-family sites showing all trees ≥4 inches DBH location, species, size, and condition.
Protected Trees: Generally any tree ≥8 inches DBH; Grand/Historic Trees (≥18 inches DBH for most species) receive greatest protection.
Tree Removal Permit: Required from Pasco County before clearing. Submit tree survey + site plan showing preservation areas.
Mitigation: Removed protected trees must be mitigated via:
  (a) Replacement planting on-site (caliper-for-caliper or per Pasco LDC ratio); or
  (b) Payment into Pasco County Tree Bank at current fee schedule per caliper inch removed.
Preservation Credit: Preserved trees in protected/conservation areas can receive density/open space credit.
Contact: Pasco County Environmental Lands / Natural Resources: (727) 847-8137.
water:
Pasco County Utilities (PCU) — Primary water provider for most of unincorporated Pasco County.
Contact: (727) 847-2411 | pascogov.com/pcu
Availability: Water availability letter from PCU required before site plan approval. Verify capacity and main size for the specific address.
Connection: Water meter sizing and tap fee determined by demand (GPM/ERU). Contact PCU for current connection fee schedule.
Note: Some rural areas are served by private wells with Pasco County Health Department oversight.
sewer:
Pasco County Utilities (PCU) — Sanitary sewer provider for most served urban/suburban areas.
Contact: (727) 847-2411 | pascogov.com/pcu
Availability: Sewer availability letter from PCU required before site plan. Rural/low-density areas may use OSTDS (septic) with Pasco County Health Department approval.
Lift Stations: Developer may be required to install and convey a lift station to PCU if gravity service is not feasible.
FDEP: Domestic wastewater collection/transmission system extension: Notice of Intent (NOI) required.
reclaim:
Pasco County Utilities provides reclaimed water service in designated service areas.
Reclaimed water irrigation is required on commercial sites within PCU-served areas per Pasco County Comprehensive Plan water conservation policies.
Contact PCU for service area map and availability: (727) 847-2411.
Irrigation system design must separate reclaimed and potable water; cross-connection prevention required (FDEP backflow standards).
gas:
Peoples Gas (a TECO Energy company) serves portions of Pasco County.
Contact: (877) 832-6747 | peoplesgas.com
Gas service availability varies by location — verify with Peoples Gas before design. Natural gas is not available in all parts of Pasco County; propane may be used in rural areas.
electric:

2379 Broad Street, Brooksville, FL 34604 | 1-800-423-1476 | swfwmd.state.fl.us
